# `dsh.profile.bundles`; see `dsh.bundle` in the repository package.json.

# One row: the plugin mounts the skill provider and the Employed MCP server itself,

      name: "employed-dsh/.dsh-plugin/index.mjs"

readme.section: Employed by Guaq AI for DeepSeek Harness
readme.text:
Live job search for [DeepSeek Harness](https://dsh-plugin.org) (dsh): search roles verified on about 5,000 employer applicant-tracking boards, open an employer's hiring profile, and brief a hiring market, from inside a dsh session.

This bundle mounts two things:

- the Employed skills (`skills/`), as an isolated skill provider;
- the remote Employed MCP server, `https://jobs.guaqai.me/mcp`, over Streamable HTTP.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Guaq-AI/employed-dsh
```

Then, inside a session, store your API key (create one at <https://jobs.guaqai.me/profile>):

```text
/employed-login <api-key>
```

dsh's MCP client has no OAuth flow, so this bundle signs in with an API key kept in dsh's credential store. The key is never written to this package or to the session log, and it is sent only to `https://jobs.guaqai.me/mcp`.

- **Category:** Integrations & Connections.
- **Compatibility:** DeepSeek Harness with the `web` profile; the bundle is an ES module that exports `apply(ctx)` and uses dsh's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`. Any platform dsh runs on.
- **Permissions and external services:** one outbound connection, to `https://jobs.guaqai.me/mcp`, carrying the search filters the model chooses and your API key as a Bearer token. Account tools change only your own Employed data (profile, tracker, alerts), and only when you ask; nothing applies to jobs or contacts employers. No hooks, no shell commands, no files written.
- **Example prompts:** "Find entry-level backend roles in India." "Is Stripe hiring in London right now?"
- **Known limitations:** dsh's MCP client has no OAuth, so sign-in is by API key. Not yet run against a live dsh build; please open an issue if anything fails.
Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI and the rest install from [Guaq-AI/employed-plugins](https://github.com/Guaq-AI/employed-plugins), which signs in with OAuth instead of an API key.
